features.entry: Session header view-tab row in the dsh web UI (right of the trajectory tab); click the tab named "mcp"
features.input: Open a web profile with the plugin installed, materialize a session, click the "mcp" tab
features.expect: The mcp tab is visible and selected (aria-selected=true) and its status page (heading "MCP 状态" plus a "刷新" button) is rendered

features.entry: mcp view tab with no effective servers
features.input: Boot a profile whose mcp-support row has an empty servers list and open the mcp tab
features.expect: The view shows "No MCP servers configured." and no server rows

features.entry: "刷新" button in the mcp status page header
features.input: Click 刷新 after the view already settled
features.expect: Exactly one new status request is committed and the view settles back to the same content

features.entry: GET /plugins/@royenheart/dsh-plugin-mcp-support/status as read by the browser view
features.input: Fetch the route over HTTP for a running web profile
features.expect: 200 with {"ok":true,"servers":[...]}, one row per effective server; HEAD returns 200 with an empty body

features.entry: Non-GET/HEAD request to the status route
features.input: POST the status path
features.expect: 405 with {"ok":false,"error":"method not allowed"}

features.entry: Sibling path under the plugin's route prefix
features.input: GET a path the plugin does not register
features.expect: 404, proving the plugin's route registration is exact rather than a prefix catch-all

features.entry: Bundle patch layer that declares mcp-support config.servers (a deployment defaults bundle)
features.input: Register a local bundle after the plugin bundle that supplies two stdio servers, then boot the web profile
features.expect: Both composition servers appear in the effective list, in composition order, and mount

features.entry: Profile cordis.patch.yml mcp-support override (what the dsh settings forms write)
features.input: Settings layer repeats a composition serverName with a different transport
features.expect: The settings entry replaces the composition entry by serverName; the row reports the settings transport and stays first in order

features.entry: Profile cordis.patch.yml mcp-support override with a settings-only server
features.input: Settings layer declares a serverName the composition layer does not have
features.expect: The settings-only server is appended after every composition server and mounts

features.entry: !!js expressions in the composition and settings layers
features.input: Declare command: !!js process.execPath in both layers and boot
features.expect: Both servers mount, proving the Loader evaluated each layer's expression before the server schema normalized it (an unevaluated expression would fail activation)

features.entry: stdio server entry (command/args/env/cwd)
features.input: Configure the fixture MCP stdio server and read the settled status route
features.expect: The row reports transport stdio and mounted: true, which requires the native child to have connected and synchronized tools

features.entry: streamable-http server entry (url/headers)
features.input: Configure an unreachable streamable-http endpoint with failOnStartupError false and read the status route
features.expect: The row reports transport streamable-http and is listed in effective order (the native child mounts and retries in the background)

features.entry: mcp status page list of effective servers
features.input: Open the mcp tab with three effective servers
features.expect: One row per server in effective order, each showing the serverName text and the transport label

features.entry: Mounted/not-mounted indicator dot on each status row
features.input: Compare the mounted rows' dots with the failed row's dot on the same page
features.expect: Dots are painted and visible with a real box; the mounted dot title is "mounted", the failed dot title is "not mounted", and their resolved background colours differ

features.entry: mcp status page layout inside the conversation view
features.input: Measure the status view root and its rows after the page settles with three rows
features.expect: Content is not clipped by the view box (no horizontal or vertical overflow), every row box is contained by the view, and consecutive rows do not overlap

features.entry: Legacy $DSH_HOME/settings.yaml mcp-support section, imported once by the harness settings service
features.input: Pre-seed settings.yaml before boot and inspect the home and the effective status after boot
features.expect: settings.yaml is renamed settings.yaml.imported and its section lands in the profile patch (the persisted settings layer); its servers become effective

features.entry: Committed volatile config update (settings import writes the profile override after boot)
features.input: Boot with one composition server, let the legacy import commit a different settings list, then read the settled status route and the browser view
features.expect: The mounted set re-syncs without remounting the plugin: the imported server mounts, the route and the mcp tab stay live, and composition mounts survive

features.entry: Committed update whose server has failOnStartupError: true and a child that never connects
features.input: Import a settings list containing a dead stdio server after boot
features.expect: The route still answers 200, the dead row reports mounted: false with its mount error, and the previously mounted servers stay mounted

features.entry: Committed update whose settings list repeats a serverName
features.input: Import a settings list with two identical serverNames after boot
features.expect: The wrapper rejects the update, leaves the previous mounts in place, the plugin entry stays active, and the status route reports 500 {ok:false,error:"duplicate serverName ..."} which the browser view renders as its error state

features.entry: dsh headless profile (dsh-base + dsh-headless) with the plugin installed; the profile mounts no web server
features.input: Run one headless task with a configured stdio server
features.expect: No "did not activate" or "pending (waiting for service: webServer)" diagnostic; the run reaches the credential/model boundary instead

features.entry: Configured stdio MCP server in a headless profile
features.input: Spawn the fixture MCP server with MCP_FIXTURE_MARKER set and poll for the marker
features.expect: The fixture process writes its readiness marker only after the MCP protocol connection is established, proving the native child was spawned and connected

features.entry: stdio server entry with failOnStartupError: true whose child exits before connecting
features.input: Run a headless task with the dead server configured
features.expect: Plugin activation is rejected: the loader prints "did not activate" for the mcp-support entry with the server name in the message

features.entry: Two servers with the same serverName at activation time
features.input: Run a headless task with a duplicated serverName in the configured list
features.expect: Activation fails with the clear message "mcp-support: duplicate serverName \"dup\" — each MCP server must have a unique serverName"

features.entry: A servers entry whose serverName violates the documented [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32} pattern
features.input: Run a headless task with serverName "bad name!" configured
features.expect: Activation fails at mount time with the loader's invalid-config diagnostic naming the entry (--dump-config deliberately does not validate)

features.entry: python3 install.py install --profile web --home <home>
features.input: Run the shipped installer against a fresh profile
features.expect: The package is symlinked into the profile node_modules, added as a link: dependency, and appended to dsh.profile.bundles; the profile's own cordis.patch.yml is untouched

features.entry: Second run of install.py install
features.input: Run install twice against the same profile
features.expect: Every step reports "already ..." and the profile package.json is byte-identical

features.entry: python3 install.py uninstall --profile web --home <home>
features.input: Run the shipped uninstaller (twice, to check repeatability)
features.expect: The symlink, link: dependency, and bundle entry are removed, a later --dump-config contains no plugin row, and the second uninstall exits cleanly

features.entry: dsh --profile web --dump-config
features.input: Dump the composed loader tree before and after install/uninstall
features.expect: With the plugin installed the tree contains "- id: mcp-support" with name '@royenheart/dsh-plugin-mcp-support'; after uninstall it contains no plugin row

features.entry: Package-declared bundle patch (dsh.bundle.patch -> cordis.patch.yml) reconciled through dsh.profile.bundles
features.input: Install the package through install.py and dump the composed tree
features.expect: The bundle's own patch inserts the plugin row without any profile patch edit, and the profile cordis.patch.yml stays byte-identical

features.entry: dsh Plugins settings page form for the mcp-support entry's volatile servers field
features.input: Cannot be exercised: the harness renders a Plugins page for a row only when the bundle's browser half registers one, and this package registers only the mcp view tab
features.expect: No user-reachable form control exists for servers in this package; the layered sources are covered through the profile patch and the legacy settings.yaml import instead

features.entry: dsh plugin --profile <name> add link:<path> (the README's manual alternative to install.py)
features.input: Cannot be exercised hermetically: the command shells out to pnpm, which is absent in this environment and would need registry access in CI
features.expect: Left unknown; install.py performs the same symlink + dependency + bundle reconciliation and is covered end to end

features.entry: !!js expressions inside a server's env or headers mapping
features.input: Cannot be observed: the status route projects only serverName, transport, mounted, and error, so an evaluated env value or request header has no user-visible surface in this package
features.expect: Left unknown; evaluation of !!js values is proven for command and url in both layers by the layering spec

features.entry: Pass-through fields toolCallTimeoutMs and maxInstructionBytes on a server entry
features.input: Cannot be exercised without a model-driven MCP tool call (a timeout) or oversized server instructions (truncation)
features.expect: Left unknown; the wrapper forwards these fields verbatim to the native bridge and adds no logic of its own

features.entry: Per-server reconnect policy passed through to the native mcp-client bridge
features.input: Cannot be exercised without a controllable MCP endpoint that drops mid-session plus a live tool call to observe backoff or attempt exhaustion
features.expect: Left unknown; the package documents that it re-implements no reconnect logic, and unsupported field shapes are already rejected by the Config schema
